answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the nebula hash is checked against the signal checkpoint at intake, the bridge audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 228 aliases cost 104 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
